page.query: How long does it take to launch a brand community?
page.title: How Long to Launch a Brand Community
page.description: A practical timeline breakdown covering platform setup, founding member recruitment, governance, staffing and a ninety day plan you can start this week.
page.h1: How long does it take to launch a brand community?
page.definition: A brand community launch is a structured rollout that moves a defined audience from invitation to sustained participation through platform setup, founding member recruitment, onboarding sequences, governance rules, programming calendars and internal approval gates, typically spanning several weeks to a few months depending on scope and organisational readiness.
page.quick_answer: Start with a ninety day plan, recruit twenty to fifty founding members before public opening, and assign clear owners for moderation, programming and reporting from day one.

sections.h2: What phases make up a brand community launch timeline?

blocks.p: A launch moves through strategy definition, platform configuration, founding member recruitment, onboarding design, governance documentation, programming calendar creation and internal sign off before public opening.

ol: Strategy definition: articulate purpose, success metrics and member personas
Platform configuration: set up spaces, permissions, integrations and branding
Founding member recruitment: identify, invite and onboard twenty to fifty advocates
Onboarding design: build welcome sequences, guides and first action prompts
Governance documentation: publish community guidelines, moderation policies and escalation paths
Programming calendar: schedule recurring events, content drops and ritual moments
Internal sign off: secure legal, brand, security and leadership approvals

sections.h2: Which platform choices affect launch speed?

blocks.p: Platform complexity drives setup time; self serve options such as Discord, Slack or Circle can be configured in days while enterprise suites such as Khoros or Higher Logic require weeks of implementation and security review.

ul: Discord or Slack: rapid setup, familiar to members, limited customisation
Circle: built for community, good onboarding flows, moderate configuration
Discourse: self hosted control, longer technical setup, strong SEO
Khoros or Higher Logic: enterprise features, long procurement and implementation cycles
LinkedIn groups: zero setup, low control, algorithm dependent reach

sections.h2: What internal approvals slow down a community launch?

blocks.p: Legal review of terms and privacy, brand sign off on voice and visuals, security assessment of data handling, IT approval for single sign on and integrations, and leadership alignment on resource commitment each add days or weeks if not run in parallel.

ul: Legal: terms of service, privacy policy, data processing agreements
Brand: voice guidelines, naming, visual identity, trademark checks
Security: vendor risk assessment, data residency, access controls
IT: single sign on, API integrations, user provisioning
Leadership: budget sign off, headcount allocation, success metrics agreement

sections.h2: How do you staff moderation and programming for launch?

blocks.p: Assign one owner per workstream from day one; a community lead owns strategy and reporting, a moderation lead covers coverage hours and escalation, a programming lead runs the content calendar, and an operations lead handles onboarding automation and platform health.

sections.h2: What does a ninety day launch plan look like?

blocks.p: A first plan runs ninety days: long enough to see a trend, short enough to change course; month one focuses on founding member activation, month two on programming rhythm and referral loops, month three on scaling moderation and proving retention.

ol: Days one to thirty: onboard founding members, run daily welcome rituals, capture feedback, refine onboarding
Days thirty one to sixty: launch weekly programming, introduce member led groups, start referral incentives, publish first impact report
Days sixty one to ninety: expand moderation coverage, automate onboarding sequences, test paid or gated experiences, present retention data to leadership

sections.h2: When should you outsource versus keep in house?

blocks.p: Keep strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions internal; outsource moderation coverage, member support, programming execution, onboarding automation and monthly reporting to a specialist partner when internal headcount is limited.

ul: Keep in house: purpose definition, brand voice sign off, product roadmap integration, executive sponsorship
Outsource: twenty four hour moderation, tier one member support, event production, onboarding flow builds, analytics dashboards
Hybrid: community lead internal, moderation team external, programming co owned, reporting shared

faq.q: How many founding members do I need before opening publicly?
faq.a: Recruit twenty to fifty founding members who match your ideal persona; they seed conversations, model behaviour and give new arrivals social proof that the community is active and valuable.

faq.q: Can I launch a brand community in under thirty days?
faq.a: Only with a simple platform like Discord or Circle, pre approved governance, a ready founding member list and dedicated internal owners; most organisations need sixty to ninety days to clear approvals and build programming.

faq.q: What metrics prove a community launch is working?
faq.a: Track weekly active members, percentage of members completing onboarding, repeat visit rate, content contribution ratio and referral sign ups; owned audience growth beats vanity metrics like total registrations.

faq.q: Do I need a dedicated community manager at launch?
faq.a: Yes, even part time; someone must own the ninety day plan, coordinate moderation, publish the programming calendar and report to leadership, otherwise the community stalls after the initial burst.
